name: CivilQuants
description: CivilQuants turns parametric inputs into audit-traceable Bills of Quantities for civil engineering assemblies — culverts, manholes, retaining walls, pavements, drainage, earthworks — across four UK measurement standards (CESMM4, NRM2, SMM7, MMHW). Every quantity traces back to its formula, and you can export to Excel, DXF and PDF. Beyond the 46 calculators, paid subscribers get ten senior-QS methodology prompts — tender review, risk assessment, measurement and contract advice, geotechnical interpretation and more — run against your own documents. Six assemblies are free; built by a working quantity surveyor.

_published_faq.name: How do I add CivilQuants to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add CivilQuants to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://api.civilquants.com/mcp. This server requires OAuth, so complete the login prompt after you connect.

_published_faq.name: What tools does the CivilQuants MCP server provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: CivilQuants lists 53 MCP tools, including compute_anchored_wall, compute_attenuation_tank, compute_bored_pile_wall, compute_box_culvert, compute_cantilever_wall, compute_carrier_pipe_run, compute_catchpit, compute_combined_services_trench, compute_connection_to_existing, compute_counterfort_wall, compute_ditch, and compute_edge_drain.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to CivilQuants?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to CivilQuants in business-productivity on the Manufact MCP catalog include Pyth, Domhaul, Idiolect AI, aster-share, and aquent-jobs.
CivilQuants requires authentication. Connect it in Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor and complete the OAuth login prompt.
CivilQuants is developed by Ember Forge Pte Ltd. It is listed as community on the Claude connector directory.
